sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the parties.

2. The petitioner in this application prays for grant of anticipatory bail apprehending his arrest in connection with Vaishali P.S. Case no.165 of 2024 registered for the offence punishable under sections 420, 419, 467, 468 and 471 of the Indian Penal Code and sections 3 and 4 of the Bihar Conduct of Examination Act.
3. As per allegation in the F.I.R, on information having been received about some persons impersonating and giving examination of NEET (UG) 2024 in place of others, a raid was conducted.

It is stated that one Dablu Kumar was caught impersonating and on being questioned he disclosed that he was giving examination in place of the petitioner herein.
4.

Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.73489 of 2024(2) dt.11-11-2024 from the contents of the FIR it would transpire that the petitioner was neither caught at the place of occurrence nor any incriminating article recovered from his possession.
He has been falsely implicated in the case.
The allegation levelled in the FIR are categorically denied.
The petitioner has no criminal antecedent.
5. The application for bail is opposed by learned APP for the State.

sentences.text: Having heard learned counsel for the parties and taking into consideration the allegation in the F.I.R. together with the petitioner not having any criminal antecedent, it is directed that the petitioner, above named, in the event of his arrest or surrender before the learned Court below within a period of four weeks, be released on anticipatory bail in connection with Vaishali P.S. Case no.165 of 2024 on furnishing bail bond of Rs.10,000/- (Rupees Ten Thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Vaishali at Hajipur.
